You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: HEAD responses served through http.ServeContent (or with no Content-Length) get a strong ETag computed from the empty body.

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Hijack after a buffered write loses the status line and headers. Probe: handler does `w.Write("PREFIX")`, then `Hijack()`, then writes "RAW" to the conn, over a real httptest.NewServer. Plain net/http sends `HTTP/1.1 200 OK ... RAW`. With ETag the wire is only `"RAW"`, so the response is not valid HTTP. The fix is to commit before handing out the conn, or to mark the writer hijacked. Reproduced.
- [blocking] Every hijack (for example a websocket upgrade over GET) logs two server errors. Cause: `finish` calls `commit`, which calls `WriteHeader(200)` and `Write` on the hijacked conn. Server log: `http: response.WriteHeader on hijacked connection from ...commit (etag.go:99)` and `http: response.Write on hijacked connection from ...commit (etag.go:101)`. Reproduced with Hijack and no prior write.
- [minor] GET 200 with `Content-Length: 5` and an empty body gets no ETag. Criterion 2 requires an ETag on GET with an empty body, and the length exemption was meant for HEAD only. The response is malformed anyway. Reproduced.
- [minor] Headers set after `WriteHeader(200)` or `Write` reach the client. Plain net/http ignores them, and the wrapper sends `X-Late: 1`. Reproduced.
- [minor] The panic path is the same as plain net/http, so it is not a regression. Under `ETag(Recoverer(h))` a panic after a partial write produces a complete 200 with ETag. Plain net/http yields the same 200 with the partial body. Not reproduced as a regression.
=== REVIEW 2 FINDINGS ===
- [minor] Hijack after a buffered write, where the underlying Hijack then fails, still sends the status and body (commit() sets `committed` before the error is known). The response then goes out with no ETag, and finish() is skipped. Reproduced: a wrapper whose Hijack returns io.ErrClosedPipe gave `code=200 body="body-tail" etag=""`. The body is correct, so this is a degradation, not a correctness failure.
- [minor] The ETag doc comment on the type does not mention that Hijack also stops buffering, unlike Flush. Not reproduced as a defect; a doc-completeness nit.
=== IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 1 (sent after review 1) ===
Fix round 1 for an uncommitted change in /tmp/ff-eval-69rk39s7/workspace: new middleware/etag.go (ETag middleware: buffers GET/HEAD 200 bodies in etagResponseWriter, adds a body-derived ETag, and answers 304 on If-None-Match) and middleware/etag_test.go. Read both first.

GOAL: fix two reproduced blocking findings in the Hijack path. Both have the same cause.
1. Hijack after a buffered write drops the status line and headers. A handler does w.Write("PREFIX"), then Hijack(), then writes "RAW" to the conn over a real httptest.NewServer. Plain net/http puts `HTTP/1.1 200 OK ...` and PREFIX on the wire before RAW. With ETag the wire is only "RAW".
2. After every successful hijack (e.g. a websocket upgrade over GET), finish→commit calls WriteHeader and Write on the hijacked conn. The server logs `http: response.WriteHeader on hijacked connection` and `response.Write on hijacked connection`.

Fix: in Hijack, when the underlying writer is an http.Hijacker, first commit() if ew.wroteHeader, so the buffered status, headers and body reach the underlying writer the way net/http sends them. Then call the underlying Hijack, and on success make sure finish() does nothing (setting committed=true is enough). If the underlying writer isn't a Hijacker, keep returning the existing "chi/middleware: http.Hijacker is unavailable on the writer" error and leave the state alone. Keep the change minimal. Change nothing else in etag.go.

FILES: middleware/etag.go, middleware/etag_test.go. Don't touch README.md, FEATURE_FLOW.md or other files.

Tests to add in etag_test.go, over a real server (httptest.NewUnstartedServer with Config.ErrorLog = log.New(&buf, "", 0), then Start; use a raw TCP client: net.Dial to the server address, write "GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\n\r\n" by hand, and read the conn until EOF with a deadline):
(a) write-then-hijack: the wire starts with "HTTP/1.1 200 OK" and has PREFIX before RAW.
(b) hijack with no prior write: the wire is exactly what the handler wrote, and the ErrorLog buffer has no "hijacked connection" text.
Close the conn in the handler after writing so the client reads EOF. Use a mutex or sync wait if needed for the race detector when reading buf.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. `func ETag(next http.Handler) http.Handler` exists in middleware/etag.go with a doc comment.
2. GET/HEAD 200 without an ETag gets a strong body-derived ETag; same body gives the same tag, a different body a different tag; body and status unchanged.
3. A handler-set ETag is kept as-is.
4. An If-None-Match match on a GET/HEAD 200 gives 304, empty body, ETag/Cache-Control kept, Content-Type/Length/Encoding removed.
5. RFC 9110 weak comparison, lists, `*`, and the malformed-input cases already tested.
6. HEAD rules as already tested.
7. Other methods get the original writer.
8. Non-200 responses pass through unchanged.
9. Unwrap/Hijack/Push are forwarded like compress.go. Flush commits without an ETag and streams. Hijack commits what was already written and leaves finish nothing to do.
10. The first WriteHeader wins; 1xx passes through.
13. `go test -race ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass, and `gofmt -l .` prints nothing.

CHECKS: `go test -race -count=1 -run ETag ./middleware`, then `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .`.
